question: A song runs past the end of your cut. How long should the video be?
context: Found by running a cut to ninety seconds and adding a three minute song: the edit became 2:59 and the export would be half blank picture. Pictures: queue/manager/shots/2026-10-08-0640-music-past-the-cut.png and 2026-10-08-0640-export-says-2-59.png.

options.label: The song stops with the picture
options.summary: When you add a sound that runs past the last clip, it is shortened to end where the picture ends, with a two second fade out. The video stays ninety seconds. Drag the end of the song out again if you want the extra.
pros: What you cut is what you export, with no extra step
cons: The app shortens something you added without asking
An outro that is sound only needs a drag to bring back
options.mitigation: Only a sound added under an edit that already has pictures is shortened, the fade is plain to see on its bar, and one Undo puts it back whole.

options.label: The video ends at the last picture
options.summary: The song stays its full length on the timeline, drawn faded past the last clip. The title bar, playback and the Export sheet stop where the picture stops. Drag a clip further out and the video grows.
pros: A long song can be slid around and the video never grows by accident
cons: A sound-only intro or outro is never exported
The song ends abruptly unless you add a fade
options.mitigation: The part past the picture is drawn faded so you can see it will not be in the video.

options.label: Keep it as it is
options.summary: The video runs as long as its longest track, as in Premiere. Trim the song yourself, for example with the playhead at the end of the picture and W.
pros: Nothing new to learn for an editor
cons: Ninety seconds of song over a blank picture unless you notice
The Export sheet length is the only clue
